- `core.align_is_idempotent` — Aligning already aligned objects changes nothing.
- `core.align_then_add` — a + b under arithmetic_join=J equals xr.align(a, b, join=J) followed by +.
- `core.concat_of_split` — Concatenating consecutive slices of an array along a dimension returns the array.
- `core.groupby_map_identity` — groupby(...).map(lambda d: d) returns the original object.
- `core.keep_attrs` — A reduction with keep_attrs=True keeps the attrs unchanged.
- `core.reduce_ignores_transpose` — A reduction along a named dimension gives the same values after transpose.
- `core.sortby_reindex` — Sorting by a coordinate and reindexing to the original order returns the original.
- `rolling.equals_construct` — A rolling reduction equals the same reduction over rolling(...).construct(...), for every window that holds window valid values.

## Lattices

### `groupby.contract`

What a groupby reduction promises on every compute path. The reference is NumPy applied to each group by hand. any and all treat NaN as true, as np.any does. min_count applies only when skipna is true or defaults to true for the dtype, as the docstrings say.

| `any_all_match_numpy` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `min_count_follows_skipna` | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

### `rolling.contract`

What a rolling or cumulative reduction promises on every compute path. The reference is NumPy applied to each window by hand. argmin and argmax must return the first matching index inside the array, as np.argmin does.
